name: A Forbidden Three-Core Whose Shattered Complex Forces Corners
statement: There exists a two-connected ample pc-minimal obstruction to dismantlable ampleness with $1162$ concepts, isometric dimension $26$, and minimum degree three such that every ample family on those coordinates with the same shattered complex has at least three corners. Thus preserving the full shattered complex cannot always transform an ample forbidden three-core into a cornerless ample family, even when intermediate families need not remain pc-minimal obstructions.
proof: For the fixed $1162$-concept rooted-completion three-core, take $e=10$, $I=\{15,16\}$, the other first-block coordinates as $A$, and the remaining second-block coordinates as $B$. Its duplicated square supplies the cube on $\{10,15,16\}$; its shadow has no pairs between $A$ and $I$ and none between $B$ and $e$, while the pair graphs induced on $A$ and $B$ each contain a spanning star. These are properties of the shattered complex alone. The support-pattern lemma therefore applies to every ample realization with that complex and forces $2^2-1=3$ corners in the unique distinguished cube.
